clue.text: Which might offer exotic pose? Phew!

definitions.text: Which might offer exotic pose? Phew!

indicators.note: exotic suggests something strange and foreign, so the letters that follow are rearranged unusually

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A breathless reaction to a racy display of an exotic pose.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: a PEEPSHOW is exactly the place you might see an exotic pose and say phew.
explanation.definitionFit: A peepshow is a booth or display where viewers watch titillating performances, which might well include risqué posing.

clue.text: Picture Céline finally playing in Vegas

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the singer's name
playing suggests something put into lively motion, so the following words are rearranged

blocks.note: the last letter of the name
taken as written, both words used

explanation.surface: Imagining Céline Dion performing her Las Vegas residency.
explanation.walkthrough: The little word 'in' looks like a positional link but belongs to the letters being rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To envisage something is to form a mental image of it, just as picturing something means imagining it.

clue.text: Work developing Plato’s ideas about introduction of Republic

indicators.note: developing means changing shape, so the letters are reorganised
about means surrounding, so the philosopher's words wrap around the extra letter
the introduction of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: taken as written, the apostrophe ignored
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A scholar's book building on the philosophy set out in Plato's Republic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work' is the definition, a literary work: Milton's epic poem PARADISE LOST.
explanation.definitionFit: Paradise Lost is John Milton's seventeenth-century epic poem, a famous literary work.

clue.text: Timeless Hampshire town a hotbed of revolution

indicators.note: timeless means without time, and T is the abbreviation for time, so that letter goes

blocks.note: Havant is a town in Hampshire, a county in southern England
taken as written

explanation.surface: Describing a sleepy English town as an unlikely centre of political revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: HAVANT loses its T, then A is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Havana, capital of Cuba, was the focus of Castro's revolution of 1959, making it a famous revolutionary centre.

clue.text: Lots of dosh riding on the second at Aintree, where it’s very dry

indicators.note: the second of a word is its second letter
in a down clue, one piece riding on another sits above it, so it comes first

blocks.note: a wad is a thick bundle of banknotes; dosh is British slang for money
the second letter of the racecourse name

explanation.surface: A big bet on the runner-up at Aintree, the Liverpool racecourse that hosts the Grand National.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Riding' suggests a jockey, but here it only places one piece on top of the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A wadi is a desert valley or watercourse that stays dry except during rare rains.

clue.text: Rum, lager, bed – capital! …

indicators.note: rum is an old British word for odd or strange, so the following letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A list of a great night: rum, beer, then bed, with 'capital!' as the old British cheer for excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rum' looks like a drink beside lager, but it means strange. 'Capital' looks like an exclamation of approval but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Belgrade is the capital city of Serbia, standing where the Sava meets the Danube.

clue.text: … after that, regularly sliced cheese

indicators.note: regularly sliced means cut at even intervals, keeping every other letter

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue's meal: after the drinking, some cheese is cut.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links the surface to the clue above, but the wordplay stands alone: 'after that' is the source of the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Feta is a crumbly white Greek cheese made from sheep's or goat's milk.

clue.text: Line dances failing at the first attempt

indicators.note: failing at the first means the opening letter is lost

blocks.note: taken as written
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: Someone flunking a line-dancing class on the first go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Line dances' reads as one phrase, but 'Line' is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancestry means lineage or descent, a family line traced back through generations.

clue.text: Lincoln Road regularly demeans city

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

blocks.note: Abe is the short name of Abraham Lincoln
RD is the standard abbreviation for road
the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: A street called Lincoln Road gives the city a bad name.
explanation.walkthrough: Lincoln is also an English city, a decoy here: it is the president.
explanation.definitionFit: Aberdeen is a granite city on the north-east coast of Scotland.

clue.text: Concerning secret exposed

indicators.note: exposed means stripped of covering, so the outer letters are removed

blocks.note: covert means secret or hidden

explanation.surface: Something worrying about a secret that has come out.
explanation.definitionFit: Over can mean about or regarding, as in a quarrel over money, matching concerning.

clue.text: Fancy car magazine featuring Golf – a timeless classic

indicators.note: featuring means including, so the extra letter goes among the others
fancy means elaborate or ornamental, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
G is Golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A glossy motoring magazine reviews the VW Golf, an enduring classic car.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about cars, but 'Golf' gives a single letter and the classic is a hymn.
explanation.definitionFit: Amazing Grace is a much-loved eighteenth-century Christian hymn, still sung and recorded today.

clue.text: Talk over conflict engineers new underground network

blocks.note: to rabbit is British slang for chattering on
war is armed conflict
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Military engineers negotiating about a new tunnel system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' just joins the first piece to the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbit warren is the network of interconnected burrows that rabbits dig below ground.

clue.text: Terrible racket on board airline, time for a bit of playful chat

indicators.note: on board places one piece alongside the airline, following it in the across entry

blocks.note: BA is British Airways
a din is a loud, unpleasant noise
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Noise on a flight prompts some light-hearted chat among passengers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terrible' looks like it signals rearranged letters, but 'Terrible racket' simply describes the noisy piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Badinage is light, teasing banter or good-humoured repartee between people.

clue.text: Darwin’s ship robbed of British gold coin

blocks.note: HMS Beagle carried Charles Darwin on his voyage
B is the abbreviation for British

explanation.surface: Darwin's famous vessel loses a valuable British coin to thieves.
explanation.definitionFit: The eagle was a ten-dollar United States gold coin minted from the 1790s until 1933.

clue.text: Bishop introduced to sharp German consort

indicators.note: introduced to means put inside, so one piece goes into another

blocks.note: alert means quick-witted and sharp
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A cleric is presented to a clever German royal spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Prince Albert of Saxe-Coburg and Gotha was Queen Victoria's German-born husband, the Prince Consort.

clue.text: Bottled spirit not carrying international basic code

indicators.note: not carrying means leaving something out, so a letter is dropped

blocks.note: a genie is the spirit kept in a lamp or bottle
I is the abbreviation for international

explanation.surface: A bottle of liquor without a global barcode.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottled spirit' suggests gin or whisky, but it is the magical spirit of a lamp.
explanation.definitionFit: A gene is a unit of heredity, a stretch of DNA carrying fundamental genetic instructions.

clue.text: Upright piano in coastal Indian state missing

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the music letter sits within another word

blocks.note: Goa is a small state on India's west coast
lost means missing
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: An upright piano has gone missing from somewhere in Goa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upright piano' reads as one instrument, but 'Upright' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A goalpost is one of the two vertical posts marking the goal in football and similar games.

clue.text: Debate Republican beset by fever

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded on all sides, so one piece is enclosed

blocks.note: ague is an old word for a malarial fever
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: A US politician taking part in a debate while running a temperature.
explanation.definitionFit: To argue is to put forward reasons for or against something, the same as debating a point.

clue.text: Clear Magna Carta embodies strong spirit

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word, the second, and the start of the third

clue.text: Provided initial snapshots of fiscal year, somewhat dodgy

blocks.note: if means provided that
the first letters of the two words

explanation.surface: Early figures for the financial year look questionable.
explanation.definitionFit: Iffy is informal for doubtful or of questionable quality, matching dodgy in a mild degree.

clue.text: Father taking over castle towers permanently

indicators.note: taking means holding inside, so one piece is enclosed by the other

blocks.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over
a keep is the main tower of a castle

explanation.surface: A priest takes charge of the towers of a castle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking over' looks like one phrase meaning seizing control, but 'over' is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: For keeps is an idiom meaning for good, forever, with no return expected.

clue.text: Back in Florida, Orlando’s blossoming

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: the last letter of the state
Orlando Bloom is an English film actor

explanation.surface: Back home in Florida, the city of Orlando is flourishing.
explanation.walkthrough: Orlando looks like the Florida city, but it is the actor's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Abloom means in flower, with blossoms open, so it matches blossoming as a predicate adjective.

clue.text: How one might be heading into Lea St, Wardlow

blocks.note: runs across all three words, ignoring the comma

explanation.surface: Directions for someone driving into a street in a place called Wardlow.

clue.text: A hot area in Syria periodically evacuated – it’s a desert

emptied at regular intervals, so every other letter is kept

blocks.note: taken as written
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap
A is the abbreviation for area
the first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: A hot spot in Syria being emptied of people, described as a wasteland.

clue.text: Sailor exhausted, drained, having a lie-in

the first and last letters

clue.text: River Dee flowing over aquatic plant

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for river
taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: The Dee is a real river, so the surface is a scene; 'River' gives a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A reed is a tall grass growing in water or marshy ground.
